observation.visible_scene: An outdoor basketball court at dusk (blue outer surface with a maroon key), enclosed by a chain-link fence with trees, light poles and a parking lot beyond. A glass backboard and hoop with a red-rimmed net stand on the right. A man in a white long-sleeve shirt, light grey shorts, white socks and dark slides occupies the court.
visible_changes: At the first frame the ball is seated at the rim/net and the man holds a one-arm follow-through pose, indicating a shot has just been taken (the release itself is outside the clip).
The ball then descends from the rim, falling past the backboard and net down toward the court surface over roughly the first second.
From about t=1.0s onward the ball rests on the maroon key near the right side, with only minor settling/position changes for the remainder of the clip.
The man lowers his shooting arm, shifts his stance, and then walks/jogs from the left side of the court toward the right, closing the distance to the ball.
By the last frame the man stands on the right side close to the stationary ball, facing it, but no pickup occurs within the excerpt.
The camera framing stays fixed: the hoop, fence, light pole and court lines hold constant positions across all frames, so apparent motion is from the person and ball, not the camera.
outside_clip_unknowns: The shot release and ball flight that placed the ball at the rim before t=0 are not shown.
Whether the man retrieves the ball after the clip ends is not shown.
The exact bounce/roll physics of the ball after it hits the ground cannot be determined from these sampled frames.
uncertain_details: Whether the ball bounces once or simply lands and rests is ambiguous due to frame spacing.
The man's gait (walk vs. jog) transitions gradually and is hard to pin to a single frame.
Minor apparent shifts in the ball's ground position may be small rolls or sampling noise rather than clear translation.
